output.summary: Most of the $14.5M shrink increase sits in DSD categories (73%). It follows removal of receiving clerks in 41 stores in April 2025. Clerk stores rose 1.4% to 1.7%, while no-clerk stores rose 1.4% to 3.0%. An audit found 31% of deliveries short. A reinstatement pilot with matched controls cut DSD shrink from 4.4% to 1.9%, with credits far above labor cost. Associate theft indicators are flat. The count-firm artifact is ruled out. Urban organized crime is small and unquantified. Camera upgrades showed no effect. District 4's bag-check and discipline policy suppressed shortage claims and did not reduce shrink. Locked cases lost more margin than the shrink they saved. Reinstate count-before-sign-off receiving first. Hold the LP spend until urban loss is better measured.
